proof.text: For every acyclic H, apply K-flatness of P and then Q. Use the inverse Mathlib HomologicalComplex.associator to transport exactness in every degree back to Tot(H tensor Tot(P tensor Q)). This proves independent-coefficient K-flatness with no boundedness assumption.

Convert site flatness to categorical flatness with SheafOfModules.flat_to_cat. The monoidal closure of CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat gives flatness of each P^p tensor Q^q. Transfer its right tensor exactness back along siteSheafTensorRightIso.

The degree-i term is definitionally the coproduct over the Type-0 subtype of integer pairs summing to i. Tensor preserves these coproducts by tensorLeft_preservesColimits_independentCoefficients and symmetry. Thus tensorLeft of that coproduct is naturally isomorphic to the flipped diagram of tensor functors followed by colim. Each component preserves finite limits by term flatness; colim preserves finite limits since exact coproducts of abelian sheaves transfer along SheafOfModules.toSheaf. Transfer left exactness across the comparison, then across symmetry; tensor also preserves finite colimits. Finally siteSheafTensorRightIso gives site flatness.

title: K-flat total tensor model for flat-term resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $P,Q$ be possibly unbounded, integer-indexed cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], both K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Their direct-sum total tensor $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ is K-flat and has flat terms, including when both complexes are unbounded in both directions. Explicitly, each term $T^i=\bigoplus_{p+q=i}P^p\otimes_R Q^q$ is flat. For every complex $H$ there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R T)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)\otimes_R Q),$$
whose restriction to degree $(a,p,q)$ is $h\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(h\otimes x)\otimes y$, with the direct-sum total differentials. The localized object of $T$ is the derived tensor of the localized objects of $P,Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; hence $T$ is itself a flat-term K-flat representative that can be used in a further derived tensor or derived pullback. No boundedness or flatness of the cohomology sheaves is assumed.
